title: Successive quotient normalizations under the pulled reduction comparison
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes and use the adic datum, small pro-etale sites and coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For $W=T,T'$ put $B_W=A_W$, $R_W=\underline A_W$ and $S_{n,W}=(P_n)_W$. Let $K\in D(B_T)$ be arbitrary, $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_T}S_{n,T}$, $N=Lg_R^*\operatorname{Res}_T K$, $N_n=N\otimes^L_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'}$, and $H_n=Lg_n^*K_n$. Use finite module pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and the specified finite coefficient isomorphisms $\tau_n:N_n\xrightarrow{\sim}H_n$ of [lem-weil-pbc-pulled-reduction-strict-tower-comparison].

For $b\geq a\geq1$ let $\theta^N_{b,a}:N_b\otimes^L_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}\to N_a$ be successive scalar-extension normalization [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Define $\theta^H_{b,a}:H_b\otimes^L_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}\to H_a$ by the canonical pullback/scalar-extension comparison followed by $Lg_a^*$ of the normalization $K_b\otimes^L_{S_{b,T}}S_{a,T}\to K_a$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Then $\theta^H_{b,a}$ is invertible and
$$\theta^H_{b,a}\circ(\tau_b\otimes^L1)=\tau_a\circ\theta^N_{b,a}.$$
The comparisons are natural in $K$. For $c\geq b\geq a$, successive $\theta^H_{c,b}$ and $\theta^H_{b,a}$ equal $\theta^H_{c,a}$ under canonical derived scalar associativity; for $b=a$ the map $\theta^H_{a,a}$ is the scalar-extension unit identification.

On a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], these are the derived maps induced by the balancing maps $(x\otimes t)\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes q_{b,a}(t)s$ before and after inverse image and scalar extension. The two triple-normalization composites are the map $((x\otimes t)\otimes s)\otimes v\mapsto x\otimes q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v$ under the same comparisons. These formulas specify morphisms of sheaf tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the stated comparisons and equalities hold independently of the chosen K-flat representative.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat $B_T$-complex $P$ representing $K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The flatness of $B_T$ over $R_T$ in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] implies that $\operatorname{Res}P$ is K-flat over $R_T$: for an acyclic $R_T$-complex $E$, $B_T\otimes_{R_T}E$ is acyclic, and $P\otimes_{R_T}E=P\otimes_{B_T}(B_T\otimes_{R_T}E)$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Its terms are $R_T$-flat because the functor $P^i\otimes_{R_T}-$ is the composite of the two exact tensor functors. This uses no completeness of $K$.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), together with the flat coefficient extension specified in the cited node.

proof.text: Put $P_n=P\otimes_{B_T}S_{n,T}$ and $U=g_R^*\operatorname{Res}P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], applied also to identity-topos scalar extension, $P_n$, $U$, $U\otimes_{R_{T'}}S_{n,T'}$ and $V_n=g_n^*P_n$ are K-flat with flat terms over their respective rings. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] these represent $K_n,N,N_n,H_n$, respectively. The coefficient identifications and quotient maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Thus all successive scalar extensions below are computed on these same complexes; no flatness of $S_{b,T}\to S_{a,T}$ is assumed.

Write $[x]$ for a local inverse-image generator of a section $x$ of $P$, and $[x\otimes1]$ for the corresponding generator in $V_n$. If $r$ is a local $R_{T'}$-section, write $\bar r_n$ for its image in $S_{n,T'}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pulled-reduction-strict-tower-comparison], $\tau_n$ is specifically pullback/scalar comparison followed by the finite constant-to-completed comparison. The latter is $x\otimes t\mapsto x\otimes t$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-coefficient-reduction-adjunct]; its hypotheses hold here by the flatness and finite-reduction isomorphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. The former is the ordinary balanced comparison on K-flat representatives by [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Consequently its chain-level formula is
$$\tau_n:([x]\otimes r)\otimes t\longmapsto[x\otimes1]\bar r_n t.$$
These are maps of actual sheaf tensor complexes: the local formulas are balanced and restriction-compatible, and the pure tensors determine maps by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus].

source.place: Tags 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); ordinary balanced comparison: sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback).

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] to the constant coefficient map $S_{b,T}\to S_{a,T}$ and inverse image $g^{-1}$. The ring sheaves on $T'$ are their inverse images by the constant-sheaf identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. In the orientation used in the statement, its comparison identifies $V_b\otimes_{S_{b,T'}}S_{a,T'}$ with $g_a^*(P_b\otimes_{S_{b,T}}S_{a,T})$. Follow by $g_a^*$ of the normalization in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Both arrows are isomorphisms, so this is the specified invertible $\theta^H_{b,a}$. Explicitly,
$$([x\otimes1]t)\otimes s\longmapsto[x\otimes1]q_{b,a}(t)s,$$
with inverse $[x\otimes1]s\mapsto[x\otimes1]\otimes s$. For $N$, [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] gives $(u\otimes t)\otimes s\mapsto u\otimes q_{b,a}(t)s$, the specified $\theta^N_{b,a}$.

Evaluate the two sides of the desired square on $(([x]\otimes r)\otimes t)\otimes s$. The upper route gives $[x\otimes1]q_{b,a}(\bar r_b t)s$; the lower route gives $[x\otimes1]\bar r_a q_{b,a}(t)s$. These agree because $q_{b,a}$ is a ring map and $q_{b,a}(\bar r_b)=\bar r_a$. The latter identity follows from the compatible coefficient quotient maps of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Additivity and balancing, followed by sheafification, prove equality on the whole complexes by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. Hence $\theta^H_{b,a}(\tau_b\otimes1)=\tau_a\theta^N_{b,a}$.

source.place: Explicit balancing calculation for the canonical maps in Tags 03EL and 0D6D.

proof.text:
For $c\ge b\ge a$, the route through $b$ sends $(([x\otimes1]t)\otimes s)\otimes v$ to
$$[x\otimes1]q_{b,a}(q_{c,b}(t)s)v=[x\otimes1]q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v.$$
The direct route first reassociates the two coefficient tensors and has exactly the latter value. Here $q_{b,a}q_{c,b}=q_{c,a}$ is part of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and the canonical scalar associators and their generator formulas are [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. For $b=a$, the same formula is $h\otimes s\mapsto hs$, with inverse $h\mapsto h\otimes1$, so it is the scalar-extension unit identification. The calculation before inverse image is identical with $[x\otimes1]$ replaced by $x\otimes1$; the balancing formula then is precisely $(x\otimes t)\otimes s\mapsto x\otimes q_{b,a}(t)s$. The local tensor generators determine these chain maps by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus].

source.place: Tags 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition) and 03EL, with the explicit triple and unit balancing calculations.

proof.text: For a chain map $f:P\to P'$, each formula above changes only $x$ to $f(x)$, proving naturality on flat-term K-flat models. These formulas commute with differentials because the coefficient sheaves are in degree zero and their multiplications commute with the tensor differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Scalar extension preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes and has canonical, composable resolution comparisons by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; pullback has the same property on the chosen flat-term class by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] identifies the localization of this class with $D(B_T)$. Thus the natural chain maps, their inverse maps, the square, the triple equality and the unit equality all descend through quasi-isomorphisms, and their values are independent of $P$. This proves all clauses for arbitrary $K$ in the stated derived categories.
